narrative:
The model determined that you have a 38% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were your savings situation, the status of your checking account, and the purpose of the loan. Your lack of any known savings was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Most approved applicants have at least some visible savings, whereas you fall into the unknown/none category that the model strongly associates with higher risk. This one factor pushed the prediction heavily toward bad credit.

Your checking account being in negative balance (under 0 DM) was the second most important driver. Only 12.6% of applicants are in this situation, and it further increased the model's concern about your reliability. In contrast, the purpose of the loan (furniture and equipment) actually worked in your favor. This is a relatively common and lower-risk reason compared with some other uses, so it pulled the prediction slightly back toward approval.

Taken together, the absence of savings and the negative checking account outweighed the positive aspects of your application and led to the denial.

What you should do next is focus on building visible savings and bringing your checking account into positive territory. Once those two areas improve, reapply. Many people in similar situations have successfully obtained loans after making these specific changes.
